items.title: Government can't escape responsibility: Delhi High Court on Satya Niketan building collapse
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Monday directed the Delhi government to intensify efforts to rescue students trappened under the debris of a multi-storied Paying Guest (PG) building that collapsed in South West Delhi's Satya Niketan. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia expressed anguish over the incident and warned the government that it could not wash its hands off the tragedy. " You [government] can't escape responsibility... 50 young students who are at the threshold of their lives... Majority of them are perhaps still lying under the debris, there can’t be anything more sad than this ," the Court said. It directed the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) to conduct an inquiry at the highest level to find out whether the building which collapsed was constructed with valid permission. The Court said that the civic authority must fix the responsibility of the officers for such a lapse and inform the Court about what action has been proposed against the erring officials. items.title: We will not be browbeaten: Punjab and Haryana High Court in Punjab DA case
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Monday observed that the Court will not be browbeaten by any kind of tactics and will defend the oath of the Constitution. The comment by Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra was made during the hearing of applications related to pending Dearness Allowance (DA) of Punjab government employees and pensioners. Justice Mishra, who today took oath as the Chief Justice amid a brewing controversy over the Punjab government's opposition to his elevation, was sitting on a division bench along with Justice Rohit Kapoor when he made the observation. "This Court would be governed by the rule of law and this institution will not be browbeaten by any kind of tactics. So therefore, we will go strictly as per the law. We have taken the oath of the Constitution and we know how to preserve our oath and defend it," Chief Justice Mishra said. The Court said it will neither be influenced by the submissions of the petitioners nor the government. "Either side, don't comment! You may have a lot of things to say or do, we will go by law. items.title: Mass tourism is hurting Kannur’s Madayippara, an eco heritage status can change it
items.summary: On a holiday, the road around Madayippara can become a parking lot. Hundreds of vehicles line the roadside as visitors make their way towards the biodiversity-rich laterite plateau in Kannur, drawn by its seasonal flowers, open landscape, and photographs of the place that have increasingly found their way into tourism promotions and social media feeds. But for those fighting to protect Madayippara, the crowds are a warning. The concern is not merely about litter, traffic or the inconvenience caused by visitors. It is about what happens to a fragile ecosystem when a landscape never meant to accommodate mass tourism begins attracting it in growing numbers, even as commercial projects emerge around it. Madayippara is a flat laterite hillock spread across around 365 hectares near Payangadi, about 22 km north of Kannur town. Once known mainly for its religious, cultural and ecological significance, it has increasingly become a tourist attraction, drawing visitors from Kerala and elsewhere, including tourists from outside India. items.title: ‘I was shocked’: Justice RV Raveendran disagrees with Justice Nariman on full appeal against arbitral awards
items.summary: Former Supreme Court judge Justice RV Raveendran on Sunday disagreed with Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman’s recent suggestion for a full-fledged first appeal against domestic arbitral awards on facts and law, saying such a remedy would defeat the very purpose of arbitration. Justice Raveendran said he was “shocked” by the suggestion, though he acknowledged that it reflected the frustration caused by the present state of challenges to arbitral awards. “ Imagine, out of desperation, Justice Nariman said, let us have a first one appeal, full appeal and be done with it. I was shocked. But see, that is the amount of desperation .” He added, “ If you have a first appeal, then why have an arbitration? The entire purpose of arbitration is to have finality .” Justice RV Raveendran Justice Raveendran said that if courts were given wider appellate powers, including the ability to extensively reconsider or modify awards, the distinction between arbitration and ordinary litigation would begin to disappear. items.title: Supreme Court’s recent arbitration rulings have created grave uncertainty: Retired Justice Rohinton Nariman
items.summary: Former Supreme Court Justice Rohinton F Nariman recently said that some of the Supreme Court’s recent arbitration judgments were incorrect and had created “grave uncertainty” by reopening settled questions. Justice Nariman was delivering the keynote address at the Gujarat High Court Arbitration Centre’s Arbitration Week 2026. He examined 5 recent Constitution Bench decisions concerning the appointment of arbitrators and challenges to arbitral awards. “ Here we have five recent judgments of the Supreme Court. How has the Act fared? According to me, not particularly well, because, firstly, the judgments don’t conduce to certainty . Secondly, constantly reopening closed questions again leads to grave uncertainty. Some of the judgments, unfortunately, are on the face of them not correct, in my humble submission," he said. Justice Nariman first referred to the five-judge ruling in Cox and Kings . items.title: Calcutta High Court transfers hate speech case against Mahua Moitra to MP/MLA Court
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on September 7 transferred the hate speech case against Trinamool Congress Member of Parliament Mahua Moitra from a Magistrate court to a special MP/MLA court [Mahua Moitra vs. The State of West Bengal & Ors.]. A Division Bench comprising Justice Debangsu Basak and Justice Aryak Dutt said that a regular magistrate court lacks the jurisdiction to entertain cases against lawmakers. "In the facts and circumstances of the present case, there is a complaint case as against the petitioner before us who is a Member of Parliament. Complaint registered as against the Member of Parliament was sought to be taken cognizance of by the learned 3rd Judicial Magistrate, Krishnagar, Nadia. Such Court is not the designated Court for the purpose of trying an offence against a Member of Parliament and Member of State Legislature," the Court held. Hence, it directed that the proceedings be transferred from the court of the Magistrate court at Krishnanagar in Nadia to the designated special court for MP/MLA cases situated at Bidhannagar in North 24 Parganas. items.title: Is Andar Bahar a game of skill or chance? Karnataka HC refers issue to larger bench
items.summary: A single judge Bench of the Karnataka High Court on Tuesday held that the question of whether Andar Bahar is a game of skill or a game of chance requires reconsideration by a larger Bench. Andar Bahar is a card game in which players place bets on whether a card matching a designated card will appear first on a box referred to as "Andar" or on the "Bahar" box. Justice Suraj Govindaraj today expressed doubts over the correctness of a 1977 High Court ruling, E Eranna v. State of Karnataka , in which 14 persons said to have played Andar Bahar were acquitted of allegations that they had played outlawed games of chance (wagering or betting games). In E Eranna , a single-judge Bench of the High Court had reasoned that the prosecution did not show how Andar Bahar was a game of chance. " It was not categorically proved that ‘Andar Bahar’ is a game of chance and that these accused were playing that game," the High Court had ruled in the E Eranna judgment. This ruling has subsequently been cited time and again by other Benches of the Court to rule that Andar Bandar is a game of skill rather than an outlawed game of chance. items.title: Company can face criminal trial even if guilty employee is not identified: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday held that a company can face criminal prosecution even if the investigating agency has not identified or arraigned the particular employee or official through whom the concerned company acted [Sanofi India Ltd. Vs CBI]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and Manoj Misra made the ruling while dismissing an appeal by Sanofi India Ltd against the Karnataka High Court’s refusal to quash criminal proceedings arising from a CBI case. The Court said that at the stage of considering a petition to quash criminal proceedings under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the prosecution is not required in every case to identify the specific natural person through whom the company allegedly acted. “ What the chargesheet must disclose, on its face, is that the corporation itself has committed the offence, not that it has also identified the particular individual through whom it did so ,” the Court said. It added that a company’s role could be disclosed through allegations concerning its own conduct, decisions and dealings, even without naming the individual who carried them out.
